feature: Interactive CLI AI Platform Engineering Learning Tool

topics.title: Docker Compose FastAPI hello app
topics.explanation: Spin up a minimal Python API behind Docker so you can see the classic build → image → container loop. A single `docker compose up` runs your app; `docker compose down` tears it down. This is the DevOps glue that later hosts model servers.
topics.next_step_action: Create a tiny FastAPI service and run it with docker compose inside a Pod.

topics.title: Pod, Deployment, Service mental model
topics.explanation: A Pod is the smallest scheduling unit in Kubernetes — a set of containers sharing a network. A Deployment manages and rolls out many Pods for you; a Service gives them a stable endpoint. Understanding these three primitives is the foundation for every platform task.
topics.next_step_action: Create a Pod, then a Deployment, then a Service to expose it.

topics.title: Python for ML literacy
topics.explanation: Python is the lingua franca of ML. You'll use libraries such as NumPy, pandas, and scikit-learn to load data, run simple models, and inspect results. Knowing Python well lets you build orchestration scripts like an Ollama client.
topics.next_step_action: Write a short script that loads CSV data with pandas and prints summary stats.

topics.title: ML vocabulary for platform people
topics.explanation: Model, training data, inference, and feature store are the words every platform engineer should know. You don't need to train models yourself; you need to move, serve, and monitor them reliably.
topics.next_step_action: Explain each term in one sentence using a container analogy.

topics.title: DVC data version control
topics.explanation: DVC tracks datasets and models alongside git so experiments are reproducible. You commit code to git, then point DVC at your data with `dvc add` and store artifacts in an object store.
topics.next_step_action: Run dvc add on a dataset and configure the remote storage.

topics.title: MLflow experiment tracking
topics.explanation: MLflow records parameters, metrics, and model artifacts for every run so you can compare which configuration performed best. It turns one-off scripts into auditable experiments.
topics.next_step_action: Log a few runs with MLflow and read back the tracked metrics.

topics.title: Feast feature store
topics.explanation: A feature store gives you a single source of truth for features used at both training and serving time. This consistency is what lets models behave the same in production as they did offline.
topics.next_step_action: Define a feature entity in Feast and query it with FastAPI/BentoML.

topics.title: FastAPI and BentoML serving
topics.explanation: BentoML packages your model into a portable service exposed through FastAPI endpoints. You deploy once to any runtime without rewriting the serving code.
topics.next_step_action: Export a Bento with BentoML and run it locally.

topics.title: KodeKloud 100 Days of MLOps exit criteria
topics.explanation: The P2 exit is a finished mini-MLOps pipeline plus public notes, marked by the 100 Days badge. Each lesson builds on the previous one so the final artifact runs end to end.
topics.next_step_action: Document the full pipeline in a public notes repo and claim the badge.

topics.title: KServe InferenceService manifests
topics.explanation: An InferenceService wraps a model behind a managed endpoint. You describe the container and autoscaling in YAML; KServe handles routing, load balancing, and canary traffic.
topics.next_step_action: Write an InferenceService manifest and apply it to a cluster.

topics.title: Argo Workflows training Jobs
topics.explanation: Training runs are non-trivial and long, so Argo schedules them as one-off Jobs composed of steps. This keeps training separate from steady-state serving.
topics.next_step_action: Define an Argo Workflow that runs a training Job to completion.

topics.title: GitOps model endpoint with Helm and Argo CD
topics.explanation: Argo CD keeps your cluster in sync with a Git repository. With Helm you render reusable templates, and GitOps gives you health checks and an automatic rollback runbook.
topics.next_step_action: Deploy your model endpoint through Argo CD from Git and verify rollback.

topics.title: vLLM model servers
topics.explanation: vLLM is a fast inference server for large language models. It uses continuous batching and PagedAttention to serve many requests concurrently on one GPU.
topics.next_step_action: Launch vLLM locally and measure throughput with concurrent prompts.

topics.title: RAG infrastructure
topics.explanation: Retrieval Augmented Generation fetches relevant documents before answering, grounding responses in your data. RAG infra handles embedding stores and chunking pipelines.
topics.next_step_action: Build a small RAG pipeline over a sample corpus.

topics.title: LLM gateways auth, rate-limit, fallback, token cost
topics.explanation: A gateway sits in front of models to enforce authentication, rate limits, graceful fallbacks, and token-cost accounting. It protects your users and keeps costs predictable.
topics.next_step_action: Add auth and rate limiting to a local gateway proxying model calls.

topics.title: nvidia.com/gpu device-plugin scheduling and DCGM metrics
topics.explanation: The NVIDIA device plugin publishes GPU resources so the scheduler can place jobs on nodes. DCGM exports hardware metrics that feed Prometheus and Grafana dashboards.
topics.next_step_action: Install the device plugin and expose DCGM metrics to a dashboard.

topics.title: Portfolio: MLOps mini-platform project
topics.explanation: Ship a small end-to-end MLOps platform to demonstrate the skills you've built. It becomes one entry in your portfolio story.
topics.next_step_action: Package the mini-platform with a short write-up for your portfolio repo.

topics.title: Portfolio: K8s model serving project
topics.explanation: Deploy a real model-serving stack on Kubernetes. This proves you can take a trained model all the way to production infrastructure.
topics.next_step_action: Document the deployment in your portfolio repository.

topics.title: Portfolio: LLM platform slice project
topics.explanation: Build a slice of an LLM application that ties together inference, retrieval, and gateway. It rounds out your portfolio with an integrative showcase.
topics.next_step_action: Add the project to your DevOps-to-AI Platform career packaging.
